# Pre-Implementation Readiness Checklist: Admin Mobile App

**Purpose**: A formal requirements-quality gate on `spec.md` (cross-checked against `plan.md`/`data-model.md`/`contracts/`/`research.md`) before `/speckit-implement` runs, per the constitution's "spec, plan, and tasks have been reviewed" gate. Broad coverage across all 3 user stories, not scoped to one risk area.
**Created**: 2026-08-31
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is a requirement defined for what happens to an in-progress admin action (e.g. resolving a dispute) if the admin's session/token expires mid-action? [Gap] — Resolved 2026-08-31: no spec change needed — this is existing, already-built, app-wide session handling (the dio 401 refresh-retry interceptor, `mobile/README.md`'s documented `dio_401_retry_test.dart`), not a gap specific to this feature.
- [x] CHK002 FR-005 bounds moderation to "at minimum: suspend/reinstate" — is the full set of moderation actions in scope for this delivery enumerated, or does "at minimum" leave the boundary open-ended? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005] — Resolved 2026-08-31: FR-005 reworded to a closed set (suspend/reinstate only), matching Assumptions' existing scope statement; removes the open-ended "at minimum" language.
- [x] CHK003 Is a requirement defined for what account detail (role, verification status, not just active/inactive) must be shown once an admin locates a specific account via FR-005? [Gap, Spec §FR-005] — Resolved 2026-08-31: FR-005 now explicitly requires name/email/role/active/verification status to be shown.
- [x] CHK004 Is a requirement defined for how an admin disambiguates between multiple accounts with the same or similar name when locating one via FR-005? [Gap, Spec §FR-005] — Resolved 2026-08-31: same FR-005 edit as CHK003 — email is now an explicit required disambiguator.
- [x] CHK005 Given push notifications for new disputes are now explicitly out of scope (Clarifications), does the spec define any requirement for how an admin is otherwise expected to learn a dispute exists between app opens? [Gap, Spec Assumptions] — Resolved: already answered by the Clarifications-session Assumptions edit — Story 1 is satisfied by an admin opening the app and pulling current data; no further mechanism is implied or required.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is "urgent" (User Story 1's title and framing) distinguished anywhere from a non-urgent dispute, or do FR-002/FR-003 apply uniformly regardless of urgency? [Ambiguity, Spec User Story 1 / §FR-002] — Resolved 2026-08-31: added a sentence to User Story 1 stating explicitly there's no urgency-triage tier — "urgent" motivates the story, it isn't a distinct requirement.
- [x] CHK007 Is "a quick read" (User Story 2's framing) given any objective standard beyond SC-003's 5-second alert-identification criterion, or does it remain subjective? [Clarity, Spec User Story 2] — Reviewed, no change needed: SC-003 already is that quantification (5 seconds to identify a flagged condition) — the story's framing and the success criterion are consistent, not competing.
- [x] CHK008 Is "rapid" in "rapid moderation" (User Story 3 title, Assumptions) given a measurable time bound the way Story 1 has SC-001, or does it stay unquantified? [Ambiguity, Spec User Story 3] — Resolved 2026-08-31: added a sentence to Story 3's "Why this priority" clarifying "rapid" means fewer steps than the web console, not a separate timing SLA — deliberately distinct from Story 1's SC-001.
- [x] CHK009 Does FR-008 ("MUST produce the same resulting state… never diverge") define what "same resulting state" means for fields mobile now exposes that the web console doesn't yet (e.g. the oversight alert fields)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-008] — Resolved 2026-08-31: FR-008 reworded to scope "never diverge" to shared mutated data only, explicitly excluding read-only computed fields mobile shows that web doesn't yet.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK010 Does FR-002's required detail set ("job, complainant, reason") align with the Dispute key entity's fuller field list ("the job it relates to, who raised it, its reason, its status, and who resolved it"), or should FR-002 also require status/resolver visibility for consistency? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002 vs Key Entities] — Resolved 2026-08-31: FR-002 now requires resolution status to be shown and resolved disputes to never appear actionable.
- [x] CHK011 Does User Story 1 Acceptance Scenario 3 ("who resolved it, and how") have a corresponding requirement in FR-003, which is silent on displaying the resolving admin's identity? [Consistency, Spec User Story 1 vs §FR-003] — Resolved 2026-08-31: FR-003 now explicitly requires showing which admin resolved a dispute, matching Acceptance Scenario 3.
- [x] CHK012 Are FR-004's now-quantified alert threshold (>5 failures/24h) and User Story 2 Acceptance Scenario 2's "a genuine problem exists" framing consistent — could a real but sub-threshold problem go unflagged in a way the story didn't intend? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004 vs User Story 2] — Reviewed, no change needed: this is the accepted, deliberate tradeoff of any fixed threshold, and FR-004 already frames the number as a "launch-default, tunable later" — not a silent gap.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK013 Is SC-002 ("zero disputes are ever resolved twice") independently verifiable as a requirement property, or does it rest entirely on FR-003's guard with no separate observable criterion of its own? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002] — Reviewed, no change needed: SC-002 is objectively testable directly (attempt a double-resolve, confirm the second attempt is rejected) — deriving it from FR-003 is expected, not a weakness.
- [x] CHK014 Is SC-004's "100% of moderation actions and manual payouts require confirmation" measurable given FR-005/FR-006 use open-ended "at minimum" language that could admit actions not yet enumerated? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004 vs §FR-005/§FR-006] — Resolved by CHK002's fix: FR-005 is now a closed set (suspend/reinstate) plus FR-006's single payout-trigger action — exactly 3 actions total, so SC-004's "100%" is now enumerable and checkable.
- [x] CHK015 Does the spec state how SC-005's "reflected… within 5 seconds" is meant to be verified as a requirement (vs. the 10-second refresh mechanism currently living only in Clarifications/plan.md)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005] — Already resolved in the Clarifications pass: SC-005 itself states the 10-second auto-refresh mechanism directly, not just in Clarifications/plan.md.

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK016 User Story 1's narrative mentions "approve, reject, or escalate," but FR-003 only defines approve/reject — is an "escalate" requirement missing, or was it intentionally dropped? [Gap, Spec User Story 1 vs §FR-003] — Resolved 2026-08-31: aligned spec language with the actual Dispute model (single OPEN→RESOLVED outcome, no verdict/escalate state); Assumptions now states escalation happens outside the app.
- [x] CHK017 Is an exception-flow requirement defined for a moderation action or payout trigger that fails server-side after the admin has already confirmed it? [Gap, Coverage] — Resolved 2026-08-31: new Edge Cases bullet requires the failure be clearly reported (never shown as success) and safely retryable.
- [x] CHK018 Is a recovery-flow requirement defined for what the app must do once connectivity returns after a stale-data state (FR-009) — auto-refresh, or admin-initiated retry only? [Gap, Spec §FR-009] — Resolved 2026-08-31: FR-009 now requires automatic recovery via the same periodic refresh, no manual retry step required.
- [x] CHK019 Is a concurrent-action requirement defined for two admins moderating the same account at once — the FR-005 analog of the dispute double-resolve race already covered by FR-003/edge case #1? [Gap, Coverage] — Resolved 2026-08-31: new Edge Cases bullet clarifies this is a non-issue by construction — `is_active` toggling is reversible/idempotent, unlike dispute resolution, so there's no conflicting-update race to guard against.

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK020 Is "an ambiguous or high-impact action" (User Story 3 Acceptance Scenario 3) defined concretely enough to distinguish it from every other moderation action already covered by FR-007, or does it leave an undefined residual category? [Ambiguity, Spec User Story 3 Scenario 3] — Resolved 2026-08-31: reworded the scenario to drop the qualifier entirely and state plainly there is no lower-risk subset that skips confirmation, matching FR-007's blanket requirement.
- [x] CHK021 Is there a requirement covering an admin attempting to suspend their own account or another admin's account? [Gap, Spec §FR-005] — Resolved 2026-08-31: FR-005 now excludes ADMIN-role accounts from moderation targets entirely (enforced server-side per data-model.md/tasks.md), removing the self/peer-lockout risk rather than just handling it gracefully.
- [x] CHK022 Is there a requirement covering the locate-account step (FR-005) returning zero matches, or too many ambiguous matches, to act on? [Gap, Spec §FR-005] — Resolved 2026-08-31: FR-005 now requires a clear no-matches state; "too many matches" isn't a distinct failure mode (it's just a longer, still-usable list, same as any search).
- [x] CHK023 Is the zero-open-disputes empty state's required content specified beyond "a clear nothing pending state" (edge cases), enough to be objectively verified? [Clarity, Spec Edge Cases] — Reviewed, no change needed: this is already appropriately precise for a spec — the exact empty-state copy/design is an implementation detail, and specifying it further would violate this spec's own "no implementation details" content-quality bar.

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK024 Are accessibility requirements defined anywhere for this feature? [Gap, Non-Functional] — Resolved 2026-08-31: added an explicit Assumptions bullet declaring accessibility out of scope, consistent with the rest of the codebase having no existing a11y convention — converts a silent gap into a reviewable scope decision.
- [x] CHK025 Are localization/language requirements addressed, or explicitly declared out of scope, given the platform's Tanzania market context? [Gap, Non-Functional] — Resolved 2026-08-31: added an explicit Assumptions bullet declaring localization out of scope, matching `web/`/`mobile/`'s existing English-only precedent.
- [x] CHK026 Is a requirement defined for recording which admin performed each moderation action or payout trigger, matching the level of accountability the Dispute entity already has via `resolved_by`? [Gap, Spec Key Entities vs §FR-005/§FR-006] — Resolved 2026-08-31: added an explicit Assumptions bullet stating no new audit-trail field is added this feature, and that this matches the platform's existing (also-unattributed) `/role` endpoint and automatic payout batch — not a regression introduced here, and reasonable separate future scope.
- [x] CHK027 Does the spec bound how long stale data (FR-009) may be acted on — e.g. can an admin still resolve a dispute while the app is showing a stale-data indicator? [Gap, Spec §FR-009 vs §FR-003] — Resolved 2026-08-31: FR-009 now states mutating actions are always fresh, server-validated requests regardless of list-view staleness — a stale list can never cause an incorrect mutation.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK028 The Assumptions section states "account moderation state… already exist as platform capability" — is this still accurate for suspend/reinstate specifically, given planning discovered no such endpoint existed until this feature added one? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions] — Resolved 2026-08-31: Assumptions now separates account moderation out explicitly (no endpoint or web UI existed before this feature; the web console has no account/user management page at all), and FR-008/User Story 3 Scenario 1 no longer claim parity against a nonexistent web action.
- [x] CHK029 Does the Assumptions section's push-notification language now read as consistent with the Clarifications session's explicit "out of scope" resolution, on a fresh read? [Consistency, Spec Assumptions vs Clarifications] — Resolved 2026-08-31: tightened further while fixing CHK031 below — leads with "explicitly out of scope" instead of softer "reasonable and expected companion" framing.
- [x] CHK030 Is FR-008's "never diverge from the web console" baseline checkable against a documented reference (e.g. the web console's own spec/behavior), or does it rely on undocumented tribal knowledge of what the web console currently does? [Dependency, Spec §FR-008] — Resolved 2026-08-31: FR-008 now names `web/src/app/admin/` directly as the reference for "equivalent action" — an inspectable source, not tribal knowledge.

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK031 Now that push notifications are explicitly out of scope, is Assumptions' "reasonable and expected companion" phrasing still the clearest way to state that, or could it read as reopening the scope question? [Conflict, Spec Assumptions] — Resolved 2026-08-31: reworded to lead with "explicitly out of scope," removing the softer framing that risked reading as leaving the door open.
- [x] CHK032 Is "off-cycle" (User Story 3, FR-006, Key Entities) defined relative to the existing scheduled payout cycle anywhere in this spec, or assumed as prior knowledge? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006] — Resolved 2026-08-31: FR-006 now defines "off-cycle" directly ("outside the platform's existing scheduled/automatic payout batch").
- [x] CHK033 Does the spec state an expected scale (open disputes at once, accounts searchable) for the oversight/search views, or is scale left entirely undefined? [Gap, Non-Functional/Scale] — Resolved 2026-08-31: added an explicit Assumptions bullet — no new scale target is defined; relies on the existing pagination the underlying endpoints already provide platform-wide.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify` — this file is independent of it
- CHK028 is the highest-value item here: it flags that the spec's own Assumptions text was already slightly out of date by the time planning finished (mirrors the same gap the Clarifications session found and fixed for the push-notification assumption)
